subject: English
passage: Scholars cite The Hills Were Joyful Together, the 1953 novel by Jamaican author Roger Mais, as a foundational text of Postcolonial Gothic, the Caribbean style of fiction in which Gothic conventions—often borrowed from the narrative traditions and folklore of both colonized and colonizing societies—are deployed within narratives focused on postcolonial themes typical of modern Caribbean literature. This style has exerted a significant influence on authors in Africa, including Nnedi Okorafor, whose 2014 novel Lagoon resembles classic Postcolonial Gothic novels in its integration of Gothic conventions with long-established cultural traditions—namely, those of the Yoruba people of southwestern Nigeria.
prompt: Which quotation from a literary scholar would most directly support the claim in the underlined portion of the text?

choices.A: "The cultural traditions of the Yoruba people of southwestern Nigeria, which figure so prominently in the Postcolonial Gothic tradition of the Caribbean, permit conventional as well as supernatural narratives—much as Lagoon does."
choices.B: "Although much of Lagoon conforms to the conventions of Gothic fiction, Nnedi Okorafor also incorporates elements drawn from Yoruba cultural traditions that transcend and challenge the limitations of Gothic conventions."
choices.C: "Even though Lagoon alternates between Gothic conventions and elements drawn from Yoruba cultural traditions, the influence of these cultural traditions remains constant throughout the novel."
choices.D: "Much of the interest of Lagoon derives from the productive tension between its competing influences—namely, Yoruba cultural traditions and the Postcolonial Gothic of the Caribbean."

explanation: Choice B is the best answer because it most directly supports the claim that Lagoon integrates Gothic conventions with Yoruba cultural traditions. The quotation explicitly confirms that Lagoon 'conforms to the conventions of Gothic fiction' while also 'incorporat[ing] elements drawn from Yoruba cultural traditions.' Crucially, the phrase 'transcend and challenge the limitations of Gothic conventions' demonstrates that these traditions actively engage with Gothic elements rather than simply existing alongside them, which directly supports the claim about integration.
